input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 binds Customer to use Vendor as its sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire three-year term, with no category limitation, no 12-month cap, and no performance-based exit. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback on every material term. It also conflicts directly with Section 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment), so deletion both meets the preferred position and resolves the internal inconsistency. Exclusivity running in our favour (e.g., the non-exclusive licence in 13.1) is unaffected.

proposal.summary: Delete full-term sole-source exclusivity obligation on Customer in 2.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment: our playbook does not permit exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations on us, and this clause also contradicts Sections 2.1 and 12.3, which confirm no purchase commitment or exclusivity. If Silverline needs some protection, we could consider exclusivity limited to a defined product category for twelve months that ends automatically if service levels or delivery dates are missed.
